constechr

Conservation Technology R: a shared R package of the functions ConsTech apps and pipelines use to prepare and extract conservation data, such as rasterizing an area of interest onto the national 1 km template raster or extracting national data for it.

Every ConsTech R tool calls the same function for the same task, so results are consistent and repeatable across tools. Each function documents the method it uses (CRS, area calculation, intersection rules), and tests with known answers hold that method in place.

Status

The current release is v0.2.0: reading vector layers, reading, rasterizing and aligning AOIs, polygonizing rasters, rij matrix helpers, extracting and writing layers, and the NAT_DATA and Where To Work (WTW) functions for wtw-data-prep2’s steps. The function reference for the latest release is at https://ncc-cnc.github.io/constechr/. See NEWS.md for what each release changed, docs/design/00_project_brief.md for the scope and docs/design/01_wtw-data-prep2_inventory.md for how the functions map to wtw-data-prep2.

Installation

constechr is installed from GitHub at a tagged version, so each tool pins the version it was built and tested with:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("NCC-CNC/constechr@v0.2.0")

In a project that uses renv, run renv::snapshot() afterwards to record the version in renv.lock.

Usage

Call functions with the package prefix, so it is clear where each one comes from:

constechr::function_name(...)

The example below uses the small files bundled with the package: an AOI and a NAT_DATA-like folder with a 10 x 10 template (_1km/idx.tif) and a catalogue of three layers. With real data, natdata_dir is the NAT_DATA folder and aoi your own AOI file.

natdata_dir <- system.file("extdata", "natdata", package = "constechr")
aoi <- system.file("extdata", "aoi.gpkg", package = "constechr")

# The AOI's 1 km planning units on the national template, in memory
grid <- constechr::create_1km_grid(aoi, natdata_dir)
grid$polygons

# A WTW project: its folders, then wtw-data-prep2's steps 02 and 03
# (extracting GeoTIFF layers needs prioritizr)
project_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "wtw_project")
constechr::create_wtw_project_folder(project_dir)
pu <- constechr::create_wtw_planning_units(aoi, natdata_dir, project_dir)
paths <- constechr::extract_wtw_natdata(natdata_dir, project_dir)
list.files(file.path(project_dir, "tifs"), recursive = TRUE)

The building blocks work on any template, not only NAT_DATA’s:

template <- terra::rast(
  system.file("extdata", "template.tif", package = "constechr")
)
aoi_raster <- constechr::rasterize_aoi(aoi, template)
rij <- constechr::read_rij_matrix(
  system.file("extdata", "rij.rds", package = "constechr"), template
)
rij_aoi <- constechr::clip_rij_matrix(rij, aoi_raster, template)
constechr::rij_matrix_to_raster(rij_aoi, template, aoi_raster)

The functions:

  • Building blocks: read_layer(), read_aoi(), rasterize_aoi(), align_raster(), polygonize_raster(), read_rij_matrix(), clip_rij_matrix(), rij_matrix_to_raster(), write_raster_file(), write_rasters(), extract_layers().
  • NAT_DATA: natdata_template(), read_natdata_metadata(), create_1km_grid().
  • Where To Work: create_wtw_project_folder(), wtw_project_folders(), create_dataprep_template(), dataprep_columns(), create_wtw_planning_units(), extract_wtw_natdata().

The reference for each function, including the method it uses, is in the package help: help(package = "constechr").
